description: Enforce role-based authorization on all READ endpoints and data-reading pages at the SERVER boundary, and wire student session ownership. Extends the existing OAuth role model (lib/auth/roles.ts, lib/auth/session.ts, lib/auth/staff.ts) so reads are gated, not only mutations. Preserve the no-env build invariant and demo-mode behavior when isAuthConfigured() is false.
steps: Add a shared read-authorization helper. Create web/lib/auth/read-access.ts (server-only) that reuses getCurrentUser()/isAuthConfigured() from web/lib/auth/session.ts + web/auth.ts and isStaffRole() from web/lib/auth/roles.ts. Provide: (a) `authorizeSessionRead(session)` returning a structured result { ok, authConfigured, isStaff, user?, error? } that implements: if !isAuthConfigured() -> ok:true (demo mode, reads open, preserve current behavior); else require a signed-in user; staff (isStaffRole) -> ok:true (may read any session); STUDENT -> ok:true ONLY when the session's student_email is non-null AND case-insensitively equals the authenticated user's email, else ok:false with a Spanish error; sessions with null/empty student_email are readable only by staff. (b) `requireStaffRead()` thin wrapper delegating to requireStaff() for staff-only listings. Keep all user-facing strings in Spanish. Read env only at call time.

Capture authenticated ownership when persisting sessions. In web/app/api/sessions/route.ts POST handler, before calling persistSession, resolve the current user via getCurrentUser() (from web/lib/auth/session.ts). When a user is authenticated, OVERRIDE body.studentEmail with the authenticated user's email (do not trust the client-supplied email for ownership); when not authenticated (demo/anon), fall back to the client-supplied studentEmail as today. Keep studentName behavior as-is (client may still supply display name). This is how student ownership is determined: the session's student_email becomes the owner key. Do NOT require auth to take the assessment (signed-in-or-anon both allowed) so /assessment and /g/{code} entry keep working.

Gate GET /api/knowledge (document listing) to STAFF only. In web/app/api/knowledge/route.ts GET handler, call the staff guard used for mutations pattern: since GET has no Request-token in current signature, add `request: Request` param and use authorizeStaffRequest(request) (from web/lib/auth/staff.ts) so behavior mirrors POST: OAuth staff required when configured, legacy token/demo fallback when not. Return 403 with the guard's Spanish error when not ok. Preserve the 500 error handling around listDocuments().

Enforce ownership on the results page. In web/app/results/[sessionId]/page.tsx, after loadSession(sessionId) succeeds and session is non-null, call authorizeSessionRead(session) from web/lib/auth/read-access.ts. If not ok: render the existing <AccessRestricted> component (import from web/components/AccessRestricted) with redirectTo set to the current results path and signedIn based on whether a user was present. Keep the existing 'session not found' and load-error branches unchanged. Demo mode (authConfigured false) must still render results as today.

Enforce ownership on session-reading API routes. In web/app/api/ai/report/route.ts and web/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts, after loadSession(sessionId) returns a non-null session, call authorizeSessionRead(session); if not ok, return NextResponse.json({ error }, { status: 403 }). For ai/chat where sessionId is optional: only enforce when a session was actually loaded (an unauthenticated/general chat with no session stays allowed in demo; when auth is configured and a sessionId is provided that the user does not own, return 403 rather than silently dropping context). Keep the 404 for missing sessions and the existing AI-not-configured 503.

Gate the admin evaluations/knowledge reads consistently. web/app/admin/page.tsx already calls requireStaff(); confirm listSessions()/listCohorts() only run after the guard passes (move them below the guard if needed so staff data is never computed for non-staff). web/app/admin/knowledge/page.tsx and web/app/admin/ai-settings/page.tsx already use requireStaff() - leave their gating but verify they still pass typecheck.

Add/extend tests. Create web/tests/read-access.test.ts (Vitest) mirroring the mocking approach in web/tests/auth-roles.test.ts (mock next-auth, next-auth/providers/google, @/lib/auth/link-user; mock @/lib/auth/session getCurrentUser to inject the session user; control isAuthConfigured via GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET/AUTH_SECRET env with cleanup in afterEach). Cover authorizeSessionRead: (1) demo mode (no OAuth env) -> ok true regardless of owner; (2) OAuth configured + anonymous -> ok false; (3) staff role -> ok true for any session incl. null student_email; (4) STUDENT owning the session (email matches, case-insensitive) -> ok true; (5) STUDENT with non-matching email -> ok false; (6) STUDENT and session.student_email null -> ok false. Assertions must FAIL if ownership logic is reverted (do not over-mock the function under test).
Run the four verification commands from web/ and fix any type/lint failures.
acceptance_criteria: web/lib/auth/read-access.ts exists and exports authorizeSessionRead implementing the STUDENT-ownership + staff-any + demo-open model, reading env at call time.
POST /api/sessions overrides student_email with the authenticated user's email when a user is signed in; falls back to client value when anonymous.
GET /api/knowledge returns 403 (Spanish message) for non-staff when OAuth is configured; still works for staff and in demo mode.
/results/[sessionId] renders AccessRestricted for a signed-in STUDENT who is not the owner, renders results for the owner and for staff, and still renders in demo mode.

POST /api/ai/report and POST /api/ai/chat return 403 when a signed-in non-owner/non-staff user targets a session they do not own; owner/staff still succeed; general chat without a session still works.
web/tests/read-access.test.ts passes and the full Vitest suite stays green (>= 68 prior tests + new ones).
npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npx vitest run, and (no-env) npm run build all pass from web/.
verification: cd web && npm run build   (with NO env vars set)
findings: Implemented read-access authorization. New file web/lib/auth/read-access.ts (authorizeSessionRead + requireStaffRead). NOTE: 'server-only' package is NOT installed in web/node_modules, so the module does not import it (matches existing session.ts/staff.ts convention which also omit it); the module is documented server-only instead. Wired ownership override in POST /api/sessions (authenticated email overrides client studentEmail). Gated GET /api/knowledge to staff via authorizeStaffRequest(request). Enforced authorizeSessionRead on /results/[sessionId], POST /api/ai/report, and POST /api/ai/chat (only when a session is loaded; general chat without sessionId stays open). Admin page guard order already correct (guard runs before listSessions/listCohorts when OAuth configured). New tests in web/tests/read-access.test.ts (6 cases). Verification all green: typecheck, lint, vitest (74 passed = 68 prior + 6 new), and no-env build.
